data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Apple, Nvidia, Oracle in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week as investors digested earnings reports from heavyweights including Oracle (ORCL) and Adobe (ADBE).

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the green on Friday. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) fell roughly 1% during the week. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) +23.57%
  • Coherent (COHR) +15.46%
  • Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) +14.03%
  • Corning (GLW) +13.94%
  • Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) +13.15%

Top Losers:

  • PTC (PTC) -12.86%
  • Fair Isaac (FICO) -11.91%
  • Adobe (ADBE) -11.73%
  • Tyler Technologies (TYL) -11.20%
  • Autodesk (ADSK) -10.58%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Apple launches a $2K foldable phone

After months of speculation, Apple (AAPL) took the wraps off its new iPhone models, including the iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo.

A similar size to a passport, the iPhone Duo has two rounded corners and is the tech titan's thinnest iPhone ever. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for the 256 GB option and runs up to 2 TB. Pre-orders start on Oct. 16, and it will be available on Oct. 23.

Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro sports the new A20 Pro chip and a new Camera system and starts at $1,199 and has a 2 TB option, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299. Pre-orders start on Sept. 12 and are available on Sept. 18.

“Apple is repositioning iPhone as an intelligent personal hub, with the Duo and Siri AI at the center of this strategy,” Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring wrote in a note to clients.

J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee said the event was “largely in line” with his expectations, though investors may have expected larger price hikes due to rising memory costs. (Apple also raised the price of its existing older iPhone models by $100.)

Nvidia's Huang 'confident' in 70% growth

Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang reiterated that he is “confident” in growing revenue 70% next year, adding that cybersecurity is likely to be the next major growth area for artificial intelligence.

Huang noted that Nvidia is expecting to capture a larger share of data center spending as it moves from selling GPUs into a full-stack AI factory system. The upcoming Vera Rubin system is priced at roughly $40,000, while previous systems for Blackwell and Hopper were priced at roughly $25,000 and $18,000, respectively.

Meanwhile, as per another Bloomberg report, the Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia structured its $20B licensing deal with AI chip startup Groq to avoid antitrust scrutiny.

Oracle, Adobe post quarterly results above Wall Street estimates

Oracle (ORCL) reported fiscal first-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's estimates by a significant margin.

Cloud revenue (which includes infrastructure and applications) came in at $11.6B, up 62% year-over-year. Infrastructure revenue soared 121% (120% in constant currency) year-over-year to $7.4B, while application revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $4.2B.

Adobe (ADBE) also reported second-quarter results and guidance above Wall Street's estimates. However, analysts noted a slowdown in growth to annual recurring revenue as the creative software provider pursues its freemium AI strategy.

"The quarter offered stronger adoption signals and solid near-term execution but limited incremental evidence of a financial inflection to serve as a positive catalyst," said Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Wood.

Anthropic researcher quits over AI safety fears

A former researcher at Anthropic (ANTHRO) and OpenAI (OPENAI) created quite a kerfuffle earlier this week when he quit his job and proceeded to issue a dire warning on social media regarding the imminent dangers arising from AI.

"At OpenAI, many have not deeply internalized the civilizational stakes," Jacob Coxon wrote. "At Anthropic, the stakes are well-understood, but they are locked in a race to get there first—they believe no one else will act responsibly, so they must do it themselves, despite the risk."

Other notable headlines include Qualcomm (QCOM) and Amazon (AMZN) announcing that the two companies would work together to build next-generation AI data center infrastructure.

According to a Bloomberg report, Microsoft (MSFT) plans to more than triple its global data center capacity to more than 38 gigawatts by 2032, up from about 12 gigawatts currently.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Lockheed Martin, Meta and Intel among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, after the week saw the latest consumer inflation report coming in largely in line with expectations, as well as earnings reports from companies including Oracle and Adobe.

Nasdaq (COMP:IND) and the Dow (DJI) fell roughly 1% for the week. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Lockheed Martin upgraded on earnings growth expectations

UBS upgraded Lockheed Martin (LMT) to Buy from Neutral, arguing that accelerating missile production, rising defense spending and growth beyond the company’s F-35 franchise could drive earnings above Wall Street expectations.

Analyst Gavin Parsons said he expects Lockheed’s (LMT) revenue to grow at a compound annual rate of approximately 9% through 2028, led by the missiles and fire control division. The bank forecasts companywide organic revenue growth of about 8% annually from 2025 through 2030.

The bank projects Lockheed revenue of $81.05 billion in 2026, $88.48 billion in 2027 and $96.13 billion in 2028. Its 2028 estimate is about 6% above consensus. UBS forecasts adjusted earnings of $30.69 a share in 2026, $34.50 in 2027 and $39.34 in 2028. The 2028 projection is 12% above the Wall Street consensus cited in the report.

JPMorgan upgrades Meta on AI potential

JPMorgan upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to Overweight from Neutral, citing upside potential following the social media giant’s launch of its AI assistant.

“Meta is in the early stages of releasing frontier models and AI-driven products beyond advertising, notably Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access,” analyst Douglas Anmuth said, according to reports. PT was set to $820, implying a 25% increase from last close.

“Frontier models are at the core of Meta’s (META) product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence.”

Morgan Stanley cuts Novo Nordisk rating on semaglutide concern

Morgan Stanley downgraded Novo Nordisk (NVO) to Underweight from Equal-weight, saying that the overhang from the loss of exclusivity of semaglutide remains a key concern.

“The key issue of the investment case remains Novo's reliance on semaglutide (75% of sales in 2026e), which will face a large patent cliff in the early-mid 2030s across Europe and the US. We believe that the exposure to semaglutide will remain high at the start of the LOE impact from 2031 (we model 59% of sales in 2031),” the brokerage said.

Morgan Stanley analyst Thibault Boutherin forecasts Novo’s oral obesity franchise to reach $10 billion by 2031. However, the brokerage added that it is not expecting the obesity oral franchise to fully compensate for the headwinds faced by the company.

Northland Securities says Intel made 'material progress' in turnaround

Northland Securities upgraded Intel (INTC) to Outperform from Market Perform and said the company has made “material progress” in its turnaround. 

Northland analyst Gus Richard noted Intel is likely to keep benefiting from the ongoing server CPU shortage. In addition, Intel's partnership with Tesla (TSLA) on the Terafab semiconductor endeavor will “materially benefit” its foundry business. Richard put a $120 price target on Intel.

UBS cuts NuScale Power to Sell

UBS downgraded NuScale Power (SMR) to Sell from Neutral with a $6 price target, slashed from $10, saying the company's path to secure firm customer orders orders is increasingly difficult as peers make tangible commercial progress with competing designs.

UBS analyst Jon Windham expects only 2-4 advanced small modular reactor designs to scale to meet demand for commercial electricity generation, but with competitor projects already at or near construction and NuScale's estimated five-year lead time for plant construction and lack of firm customer commitments, he believes the company's path forward is increasingly difficult.

Deutsche Bank downgraded Novartis (NVS) to Hold from Buy, citing recent failures in a pair of its late-stage trials that sent the stock sharply lower in the prior session. The analyst cut his price target on NVS to CHF120 from CHF140.

Dell Technologies (DELL) was in focus as Evercore upped its price target on the IT to $650 from $575 and kept it as a top pick, despite the recent surge in shares.

Morgan Stanley downgraded Peloton Interactive (PTON) to an Underweight rating after having it lined up at Equal-weight. Analyst Nathan Feather and his team believe that negative earnings revisions will lead to more questions on the terminal value of the stock. Morgan Stanley lowered its price target on Peloton Interactive (PTON) to $4.50 from $5.50.

data.title: OpenAI agents launched cyberattack on RubyGems before Hugging Face hack: report
data.description:
• AI agents undergoing testing by OpenAI (OPENAI) attacked software service manager RubyGems two months before the July-reported hack of AI models, datasets, and applications online platform Hugging Face. 
  • As a result, an online service for coders, RubyGems, had to stop new account registrations, The Wall Street Journal reported.
  • The cyberattack, which happened in May, was discovered by a group of AI researchers. OpenAI confirmed the event to the newspaper.
  • "Based on our review, our agents used the RubyGems platform to access the internet to carry out benign tasks and retrieve public information," a spokesperson said in a statement. "We'll continue to investigate as part of our broader review of agent activity during training and evaluation."
  • OpenAI agents are said to have used RubyGems to obtain publicly available information "as part of a training run, using the coding service as a kind of makeshift web browser in an environment where they didn't have full internet access, OpenAI said," the Journal reported.

data.title: Blue Owl, FactSet in losers; Wells Fargo, CleanSpark in gainers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street ended the week in the red after a nearly 20-basis-point jump in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) and the latest consumer price index inflation report landing.

U.S. Treasury yields jumped across the curve this week, with the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) climbing nearly 20 basis points to 4.97%. U.S. CPI inflation rose 0.4% M/M in August, matching Wall Street estimates and accelerating from July’s 0.1% gain, according to Friday’s Bureau of Labor Statistics data release.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) was down 1.46% from the previous week to $57.25.

Among megacap stocks, Royal Bank of Canada (RY) led the decliners, retreating 2.91% week-over-week to $205.90.

Mastercard (MA) (-2.82% W/W to $569.19) and Visa (V) (-2.19% W/W to $370.45) were the other notable decliners.

The week saw Ant International, Mastercard (MA), and Visa (V) launch an initiative to establish standard identification and verification for AI agents executing purchases on behalf of users.

Wells Fargo (WFC) topped the gainers in the category, advancing 1.23% from the prior week to close at $90.29.

Crypto stocks Hut 8 (HUT) (+11.93% W/W to $98.60) and IREN (IREN) (+5.23% W/W to $43.83) led the largecap gainers.

Circle Internet (CRCL) (-12.23% W/W to $90.60) and Carlyle Group (CG) (-11.33% W/W to $42.34) topped the losers in the category.

Blue Owl (OWL) retreated 10.81% to $10.56 amid fresh valuation practices concerns. The week saw the alternative asset manager slash the value of its loans to Cary, North Carolina-based specialty materials manufacturer Loparex to near zero.

TPG (TPG) was another notable loser with a 10.40% pullback to $47.69. The asset manager faced negative publicity on account of a civil lawsuit filed in Los Angeles against its subsidiary Altus Power by the industrial REIT Lineage over negligence in a fire incident.

Furthermore, TPG was also said to be evaluating the sale of its Lyric business.

Bancorp (TBBK) was the biggest loser among midcap stocks, falling 25.26% from the previous week to $50.63.

The week saw Chime Financial (CHYM) agree to acquire the nationally chartered bank and its bank partner for over seven years, Stride, for $590M in cash.

Chime had otherwise been renting the infrastructure model through Stride and Bancorp. As part of the acquisition, Chime stated it intends to consolidate its banking activities under Stride, sending TBBK stock down by about 22.33% the day following Chime's announcement.

FactSet (FDS) (-17.01% W/W to $259.71) was another notable decliner. The stock plunged on competition concerns as OpenAI announced the launch of ChatGPT for financial services. 

Digital infrastructure solutions provider and cryptocurrency miner Ionic Digital (IOND) led the gainers. The stock added 10.60% to $83.39 in a week that saw the company receive provisional ERCOT approval for 466 MW.

Another digital infrastructure platform provider and crypto miner, CleanSpark (CLSK) followed, adding 8.66% to $13.67.

Stewards (SWRD) (-21.60% W/W to $2.96), Chaince Digital Holdings (CD) (-19.23% W/W to $2.94), and Teamshares (TMS) (+18.63% W/W to $7.36) were among the significant smallcap movers.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: 5 of 6 key S&P 500 reporting firms top EPS estimates and expand Y/Y profits
data.description:
Corporate earnings featured a notable lineup of reports from 6 key S&P 500 reporting firms across the information technology, health care, industrials, and consumer staples sectors.

Earnings Roundup:

  • Bottom Line: Performance was strong, with 5 out of 6 reporting companies beating consensus EPS estimates and 1 falling short. Overall, 5 of the 6 firms delivered Y/Y profit expansion.

  • Top Line: Revenue growth was equally robust, with 5 companies exceeding Wall Street expectations and 1 falling short. All 6 companies achieved Y/Y top-line expansion.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

  • Casey's General Stores (CASY) fell 14.2% post-earnings despite posting a top- and bottom-line Q1 beat. Revenue grew 24.5% Y/Y to $5.69B (beating estimates by $140M), and GAAP EPS reached $7.37 (beating by $0.55). Management reaffirmed its full-year FY27 guidance, projecting inside same-store sales growth of 2%–5% with margins above 42%, same-store fuel gallons sold between -1% and +1%, and annual EBITDA growth of 8%–10%.
  • CooperCompanies (COO) slipped 14.7% post-earnings despite a FQ3 bottom-line beat, as a top-line miss and lowered FY26 guidance weighed on shares. Management cut its FY26 revenue outlook to $4.229B–$4.252B (vs. $4.31B consensus) and non-GAAP EPS to $4.51–$4.55 (vs. $4.63 consensus). The board also ended its strategic review by retaining CooperSurgical, citing valuation disconnects from IUD competition and litigation settlements, while expanding its share repurchase authorization to $3B.
  • Adobe (ADBE) fell 2.7% after hours despite topping Q3 estimates and raising full-year targets, as a soft Q4 revenue midpoint weighed on sentiment. For Q3, adjusted EPS reached $6.13 (vs. $6.08 consensus) on $6.76B in revenue (+13% Y/Y). Management lifted its FY26 guidance, projecting adjusted EPS of $24.45–$24.50 on revenue of $26.58B–$26.63B. However, the Q4 revenue target of $6.80B–$6.85B had a $6.825B midpoint that slightly missed the $6.84B Wall Street forecast.
  • Copart (CPRT) reported mixed fiscal Q4 results, as lower profitability offset modest top-line growth. Q4 revenue rose 2.7% Y/Y to $1.15B (beating consensus by $10M), though GAAP EPS of $0.35 missed estimates by $0.03 as net income fell 17.4% Y/Y to $327.4M. Alongside earnings, Copart agreed to acquire digital dealer auction platform ACV Auctions for $10.50 per share in cash; shares of CPRT rose 10% and ACVA surged 43% in extended trading.
  • Oracle (ORCL) rose nearly 7% after-hours following a Q1 beat and robust fiscal 2027 guidance driven by strong AI cloud momentum. For Q1, adjusted EPS reached $1.92 (vs. $1.75 consensus) on $19.35B in revenue (+30% Y/Y), with cloud revenue growing significantly. The company has $664B in total performance obligations and secured over $30B in new AI cloud contracts while completing a $20B equity offering. They expect at least $90B in revenue and an adjusted EPS of $8.10 for FY27.
  • The Kroger Co. (KR) fell 2.8% premarket despite a top- and bottom-line Q2 beat, as a lower full-year identical sales forecast pressured sentiment. Q2 revenue reached $34.6B and adjusted EPS rose 4.8% Y/Y to $1.09 (vs. $1.04 consensus). Management lowered its full-year identical sales growth outlook to 0.2%–0.8% (from 1.0%–2.0% prior) while reaffirming its full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $5.10–$5.30.

Earnings next week:

As mid-September begins, Wall Street turns its focus toward residential construction and homebuyer demand, with major homebuilder Lennar Corporation (LEN) leading next week's corporate updates.

data.title: Trump hints that trade deal with Canada coming 'fairly soon'
data.description:
• President Trump told reporters in Dublin on Saturday that he believes a deal to end the trade war with Canada could come "fairly soon" but didn't provide any details on whether talks between the two countries had restarted.
  • Trump said that he was seeking a better deal for American farmers. "Canada has to treat our farmers better, and they can’t charge our farmers tariffs. They’re charging our farmers 400% tariffs and many other things, so when those things go away, they’re willing to get rid of it all. You’ll probably see a deal with Canada fairly soon."
  • The president was asked whether the US would leave the US-Mexico-Canada Trade Agreement, but he avoided answering the question, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Nvidia a potential investor in Anthropic IPO: report
data.description:
• Nvidia (NVDA) is in discussions with Anthropic (ANTHRO) to become an anchor investor in the the AI corporation's upcoming IPO.
  • The chipmaker giant could invest as much as $10B, according to Reuters, citing sources.
  • Anthropic declined to comment to the news service, while Nvidia did not immediately respond. 
  • Anthropic is seeking to raise around $100B, according to Reuters, with a valuation close to $2T.

data.title: Costco, the Dallas Cowboys, and the art of valuing fan loyalty
data.description:
UBS drew a comparison to NFL team valuations when analyzing how investors might consider justifying the premium valuations of Costco (COST), which has smashed the return of the broad stock market over the last 20 years.

 

 

Analyst Michael Lasser highlighted that sports franchises are clear examples of how much value investors can assign to what he said were scarce, difficult-to-replicate assets with durable consumer relationships, recurring engagement, bargaining power, and multiple opportunities to monetize the same ecosystem. 

The value of the average NFL team has increased more than 30% in just one year to close to $10B. The average valuation is estimated to be approximately 13.4X revenue and roughly a high-20s to low-30s multiple of EBITDA. The Dallas Cowboys are considered the most valuable NFL franchise, with an estimated value of $16B. The future looks bright for the league as TV viewership continues to soar, apparel sales are up double digits, and international expansion is leading to new markets.

The underlying NFL assets have some key characteristics to support lofty valuations, such as scarcity, durable brands, a deeply engaged customer base, significant bargaining power, and multiple ways to monetize the same group of fans. Sound familiar? Some Costco (COST) bulls claim those same attributes exist.

Costco's (COST) professional sports franchise kinship includes approximately 145M cardholders, approximately 90% renewal rates, 914 warehouses, roughly $270B of annual sales, and $5.3B of membership fee revenue. "A Costco membership can be thought of much like a season ticket. The customer pays upfront to participate in the ecosystem. Costco then has repeated opportunities to monetize that relationship through merchandise," highlighted Lasser.

For investors, Costco's (COST) economic flywheel of membership, traffic, sales, supplier leverage, Kirkland, data, advertising, digital, and higher membership value could keep valuations churning higher as the NFL continues to see.

data.title: Boeing, engineers union reach tentative contract agreement
data.description:
Boeing (BA) ‌and its engineering union have reached a tentative contract agreement on a labor deal that includes higher general wage increases than an earlier offer that was rejected three weeks ago, union officials said late Friday.

If approved, the ~17K members of the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in ​Aerospace's professional and technical units would receive a 10% wage raise on ⁠October 16, followed by 4% raises plus merit-based increases in 2027 through 2030.

The latest offer also includes changes to work-from-home policies ​and overtime limits for professional unit members, according to the union.

The tentative deal "isn't everything we asked for, but it represents a real step forward toward improving our pay and work lives and rebuilding the relationship between Boeing leadership and our union’s members," SPEEA's ‌negotiating ⁠team said in a statement.

The current contract expires October 6, and the union could call a strike if a ​deal is not ​finalized by then.

data.title: Glencore, Mercuria pursuing Venezuela aluminum smelter deal - Bloomberg
data.description:
Miner Glencore (GLCNF) (GLNCY) and commodities ​trader Mercuria Energy are among firms interested in a ‌potential deal for Venezuela's largest aluminum smelter, Bloomberg reported Friday.

The two companies are each in discussions with the Venezuelan government about ​a deal for the Venalum smelter, and while it is not clear what structure any agreement might involve, talks have included ​operating the facility and gaining access to the aluminum ⁠it produces, according to the report.

Venalum is controlled by the Venezuelan state and was once a major aluminum producer whose output collapsed after years of under-investment, power shortages, and economic turmoil; it has a capacity to produce 430K tons/year of primary aluminum.

Glencore (GLCNF) (GLNCY) had ties to Venezuela's state-owned aluminum sector more than 20 years ago and later provided financing to the country's aluminum producers; it also built an extensive oil-trading relationship with state-owned PDVSA.
